messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high OOM rate observed on runtime pool prod-gpu-01. Error spike ~12:03 UTC. Opening incident thread — link: <https://internal/incident/4750012345>
sam: Acked. I'm oncall. Pinging runtime and infra. Starting live triage.
maria: Seeing elevated 5xx rates (503) for a subset of customers — ingests/rerank paths. Customer impact looks localized to bursty batch runs.
raj: Can someone grab `nvidia-smi` and the runtime mem stats from the affected host? I want to check fragmentation vs total alloc.
emily: Attaching quick dump from one host (shortened):
```
GPU 0: 40% used, fragmentation spikes, free contiguous largest block ~120MB
KVCache entries: total=1.2M, hot_prefix_ratio=0.28
Batch queue depth snapshot: avg_batch_size=48
OOM events: 18 in last 5m
```
sam: Hypothesis A: batch-size growth + hot prefixes caused KV cache to create many slab allocations -> fragmentation. Hypothesis B: a recent deployment toggled prefetcher causing more KV pinning.
maria: Customer impact note: support ticket INC-9982 reports ~40% increased latency and some failed uploads. Support lead notified customers and issued partial rollback to cached-routing.
support-lead: Confirmed. Impacted tenants are on dedicated pools using model variant rdx-v3-quant.
raj: I pulled pod logs — showing repeated `alloc_cuda` failures with `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` and then `fallback_swap_kvcache` triggers. Snippet:
```
[12:02:14] alloc failed size=256MB
[12:02:14] attempt kvcache swap -> success
[12:02:15] alloc failed size=512MB
[12:02:15] OOM -> evict loop
```
emily: Interesting: KV swap is being triggered repeatedly which fragments GPU address space. Also seeing many concurrent batches at ~48-64 payloads.
sam: Live mitigation proposed: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 16 for prod-gpu-01 pool, 2) enable aggressive KV eviction for hot_prefix (evict-hot=on), 3) force rolling restart of affected workers. Any objections?
maria: Do it. Reducing batch size will spike QPS tokens but should lower fragmentation.
raj: Implementing batch_size throttle now via rollout config: `runtime.batch.max_size=16` to pool `prod-gpu-01`.
incidents-bot: jobscheduler: rollout started by raj — 6 replicas at a time, 30s interval.
sam: Monitoring OOM counts and latency. Emily, can you check whether swap frequency drops after changes?
emily: Swap frequency before: ~12 swap ops/min. After batch_size change (t+2m): ~3 swap ops/min. OOM events reduced to 2 in last 5m.
support-lead: Customer errors reduced in the monitoring dashboard. Issued update to affected customers: mitigation in progress.
raj: Also found a recent PR that enabled `prefetch=true` by default on rdx-v3-quant; rolling that back in canary. Preparing a targeted rollback.
maria: Recording timeline so far: alert 12:03 -> ack 12:04 -> throttle batch 12:10 -> swap frequency drop 12:12 -> customer error reduction 12:18.
sam: Good. For RCA notes: root cause likely combination of (1) increased average batch sizes from a client traffic pattern, (2) new prefetch behavior pinning KV cache pages, (3) insufficient contiguous GPU free space causing allocation failures and chained swaps.
emily: Adding telemetry dump to the thread for postmortem: KV slab histogram, biggest free blocks, eviction counts. (pasted to logs service)
raj: Action items: A1) revert prefetch default in rdx-v3-quant (PR #5821) — owner: raj. A2) Add runtime guard to cap max_batch_size per pool when fragmentation thresholds crossed — owner: sam. A3) Improve KV eviction policy to support compaction/defragmentation — owner: emily.
support-lead: Also recommend we contact top impacted customers for timeline and compensation if SLA breached.
sam: Agree. I'll start the post-incident doc and tag people. Anything else?
maria: One more: consider adding a periodic GPU defragmentation routine (evict+compact) during low-traffic windows.
raj: Will include that in the RFC for KV cache compaction.
emily: Closing live mitigation: OOMs down to baseline, no active customer-blocking errors. Leaving thread open for RCA write-up. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident severity downgraded. Reference: INCIDENT-4750012345.
